# SQLite Gotchas

> Known SQLite patterns that cause data integrity issues or silent data loss. Load all HIGH entries before writing SQLite queries.

## Entries

- [Upsert by display name silently merges unrelated records](upsert-by-name-collision.md): Using a human-readable name as upsert key causes collisions when two entities share the same name. Use unique paths or compound keys. MEDIUM.
- [FTS5 integrity-check ignores the content table unless rank is 1](fts5-integrity-check-needs-rank-1.md): for external-content tables, `integrity-check` without rank 1 passes on a broken delete trigger; use `(f, rank) VALUES('integrity-check', 1)`. HIGH.
- [A TEXT column stores a written integer as text, so a "wrong type" fixture is not wrong](text-affinity-converts-integer-fixture.md): `SET repo = 42` stores '42' and `z.string()` still parses it, so the error path under test is never reached; corrupt with a blob literal `X'01'` and confirm with `typeof()`. MEDIUM.
- [A row that breaks two UNIQUE constraints reports only the one SQLite checks first](unique-violation-names-first-checked-index.md): a duplicate of every column reports `principals.token_hash`, not `principals.id`; violate only the constraint under test, or assert the table prefix only. LOW.
- [An audit row gated on "the change is visible" is written again when the script re-runs](audit-insert-gated-on-visible-change-repeats.md): `INSERT ... WHERE EXISTS (new state)` matches again on a second run, so a re-run SQL file logs the change twice; also require `NOT EXISTS` of the same action, target and time. HIGH.
